metadata.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (Ho, Jain, Abbeel, 2020)
metadata.framework: discrete-time diffusion process for generative modeling via iterative denoising
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:2006.11239.

nodes.name: Forward (diffusion) process
nodes.statement: A fixed Markov chain that gradually adds Gaussian noise to data $\mathbf{x}_0 \sim q(\mathbf{x}_0)$ over $T$ steps: $q(\mathbf{x}_t | \mathbf{x}_{t-1}) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{x}_t; \sqrt{1 - \beta_t} \mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \beta_t I)$ where $\beta_1, \ldots, \beta_T$ is a variance schedule. Letting $\alpha_t = 1 - \beta_t$ and $\bar{\alpha}_t = \prod_{s=1}^t \alpha_s$, the marginal is $q(\mathbf{x}_t | \mathbf{x}_0) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{x}_t; \sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_t} \mathbf{x}_0, (1 - \bar{\alpha}_t) I)$.

nodes.name: Reverse (denoising) process
nodes.statement: A learned Markov chain running backward in time: $p_\theta(\mathbf{x}_{t-1} | \mathbf{x}_t) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}; \boldsymbol{\mu}_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t, t), \sigma_t^2 I)$ starting from $p(\mathbf{x}_T) = \mathcal{N}(0, I)$. The joint reverse process is $p_\theta(\mathbf{x}_{0:T}) = p(\mathbf{x}_T) \prod_{t=1}^T p_\theta(\mathbf{x}_{t-1} | \mathbf{x}_t)$.

nodes.name: Variational lower bound (ELBO for diffusion)
nodes.statement: The negative log-likelihood is upper-bounded: $-\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}_0) \le -\mathcal{L} = \mathbb{E}_q \left[ D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q(\mathbf{x}_T|\mathbf{x}_0) \| p(\mathbf{x}_T)) + \sum_{t>1} D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}|\mathbf{x}_t, \mathbf{x}_0) \| p_\theta(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}|\mathbf{x}_t)) - \log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}_0|\mathbf{x}_1) \right]$. Each KL term is between Gaussians and has a closed form.

nodes.name: Noise prediction parameterization $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_\theta$
nodes.statement: Instead of predicting the mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t, t)$ directly, parameterize via a noise prediction network: $\boldsymbol{\mu}_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t, t) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}} \left( \mathbf{x}_t - \frac{\beta_t}{\sqrt{1 - \bar{\alpha}_t}} \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t, t) \right)$ where $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_\theta$ predicts the noise $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}$ that was added in the forward process. This follows from $\mathbf{x}_t = \sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_t} \mathbf{x}_0 + \sqrt{1 - \bar{\alpha}_t} \boldsymbol{\epsilon}$.

nodes.name: Simplified training objective
nodes.statement: The simplified objective drops the weighting from the variational bound: $L_{\text{simple}} = \mathbb{E}_{t, \mathbf{x}_0, \boldsymbol{\epsilon}} \left[ \| \boldsymbol{\epsilon} - \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_\theta(\sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_t} \mathbf{x}_0 + \sqrt{1 - \bar{\alpha}_t} \boldsymbol{\epsilon}, t) \|^2 \right]$ where $t \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(\{1, \ldots, T\})$ and $\boldsymbol{\epsilon} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I)$. This resembles denoising score matching.

nodes.name: U-Net architecture with time embedding
nodes.statement: The noise prediction network $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_\theta$ uses a U-Net architecture with residual blocks, group normalization, self-attention at certain resolutions, and sinusoidal positional embeddings for the time step $t$.

nodes.name: Connection to score matching
nodes.statement: The noise prediction $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t, t)$ is proportional to the score function: $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t, t) \approx -\sqrt{1 - \bar{\alpha}_t} \nabla_{\mathbf{x}_t} \log q(\mathbf{x}_t)$. Thus the DDPM training objective is equivalent to denoising score matching at each noise level.

nodes.name: DDPM achieves high-quality image generation
nodes.statement: DDPM with $T=1000$ steps, linear $\beta$ schedule from $\beta_1 = 10^{-4}$ to $\beta_T = 0.02$, and the simplified objective achieves FID 3.17 on CIFAR-10 (unconditional) and produces high-quality $256 \times 256$ samples on LSUN and CelebA-HQ, competitive with or exceeding GANs on certain metrics.
conclusions: State-of-the-art or competitive image generation quality
Stable training without mode collapse (unlike GANs)
Log-likelihood bounds competitive with other likelihood-based models

nodes.name: Posterior $q(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}|\mathbf{x}_t, \mathbf{x}_0)$ is Gaussian
nodes.statement: The forward process posterior conditioned on $\mathbf{x}_0$ is Gaussian: $q(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}|\mathbf{x}_t, \mathbf{x}_0) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}; \tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_t(\mathbf{x}_t, \mathbf{x}_0), \tilde{\beta}_t I)$ where $\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_t = \frac{\sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_{t-1}} \beta_t}{1 - \bar{\alpha}_t} \mathbf{x}_0 + \frac{\sqrt{\alpha_t}(1 - \bar{\alpha}_{t-1})}{1 - \bar{\alpha}_t} \mathbf{x}_t$ and $\tilde{\beta}_t = \frac{1 - \bar{\alpha}_{t-1}}{1 - \bar{\alpha}_t} \beta_t$.
conclusions: Closed-form posterior enables KL computation in the variational bound
Provides the target for the reverse process to match
